title: Infant septic shock (meningococcal)
stem: Paediatric resus. An 8-month-old boy has had a fever since this morning and is now floppy with a spreading rash. HR 195, BP 62/30, RR 52, SpO2 94% in air, temperature 39.4 °C, capillary refill 5 seconds. His mother is with him. The paediatric team is 10 minutes away.

phases.title: ABCDE
phases.goal: Monitoring on, then assess him yourself, A to E, including the rash and a glucose.

phases.title: Resuscitate
phases.goal: Oxygen, access, cultures, the antibiotic and a bolus for his weight — and his glucose.

phases.title: Reassess
phases.goal: Reassess after each bolus. Fluid-refractory? The next step.

phases.title: Talk and call
phases.goal: His mother, PICU and public health.

events.say: Reassessed: HR 185, CRT 4 seconds. Still shocked.
40 mL/kg in: still HR 180, CRT 4 seconds, cool to the knees.

review.text: Fluid bolus size. Your WETFLAGS and sepsis notes use 20 mL/kg. RCUK/ERC (2021 onwards) and NICE use 10 mL/kg, reassessing after each bolus; after 40–60 mL/kg start inotropes and involve PICU.
Antibiotic. Your notes give cefuroxime 50 mg/kg. For meningococcal sepsis, NICE uses ceftriaxone 80 mg/kg IV within 1 hour (cefotaxime in neonates; add amoxicillin under 3 months).

notes:
Checked against RCUK 2025 paediatric life support, NICE NG51 (Suspected sepsis, updated 2024), NICE CG102 (Bacterial meningitis and meningococcal disease in under 16s), and the Surviving Sepsis Campaign paediatric guidelines (2020).

Weight: APLS (age in months ÷ 2) + 4 = 8 kg.

Fluid: 10 mL/kg boluses of balanced crystalloid (or 0.9% saline) over 5–10 minutes, reassessing after each for response and overload (crackles, hepatomegaly, rising work of breathing); after 40–60 mL/kg, start inotropes (adrenaline, which can run peripherally or IO at low concentration) and involve PICU. Your notes' WETFLAGS and sepsis sections use 20 mL/kg boluses; RCUK/ERC 2021 onwards and NICE use 10 mL/kg, so 20 mL/kg is not scored.

Access: IV, and IO if IV fails in 90 seconds (or immediately in shock).

Antibiotics within 1 hour: ceftriaxone 80 mg/kg IV (NICE; cefotaxime in neonates or with calcium infusions; add amoxicillin under 3 months). Your notes list cefuroxime 50 mg/kg; that is not first-line for meningococcal sepsis.

Glucose: correct hypoglycaemia with 10% glucose 2 mL/kg (as in your notes). Check calcium. Notify public health; prophylaxis for close contacts.

steps.label: Monitoring
steps.hint: Ask the nurse to put the patient on the monitor.

opts.t: Put him on the monitor: ECG leads, NIBP cuff and SpO2 probe.
opts.mark: Asks for continuous ECG, NIBP and SpO2 monitoring

steps.label: ABCDE
steps.hint: Rapid ABCDE; look at the rash; glucose.

A B.r: Patent airway. RR 52, mild recession, clear chest.

C.t: Heart rate, capillary refill, pulses, BP
C.r: HR 195, CRT 5 s centrally, weak peripheral pulses, BP 62/30. Mottled legs.
1 cm below the costal margin (baseline before fluids).

D E.r: Responds to pain only. Fontanelle full. Floppy.

D E.t: Look at the rash; glass test
D E.r: Purpuric, non-blanching spots on the legs and trunk; they stay visible under the glass.

steps.label: Nurse
steps.hint: Access fast; bloods before the antibiotic.

opts.t: IV attempt; IO in the proximal tibia if not in within 90 seconds
opts.mark: Rapid vascular access, IO if IV fails

opts.t: Blood culture, gas, glucose, FBC, CRP, clotting, U&E, meningococcal PCR
opts.mark: Cultures and bloods before antibiotics (without delaying them)

opts.r: He is shocked with a full fontanelle: LP is contraindicated and must never delay antibiotics.

steps.label: Drug cart
steps.hint: The antibiotic within the hour, dosed for 8 kg.

opts.mark: Ceftriaxone 80 mg/kg within the first hour

opts.r: Too little for meningococcal sepsis: 80 mg/kg.
Not first-line for meningococcal sepsis: ceftriaxone 80 mg/kg.

steps.label: Drug cart
steps.hint: Fluid for his weight, then reassess.

opts.r: Current guidance uses 10 mL/kg with reassessment after each; overload is harmful.
opts.t: Crystalloid 20 mL/kg (160 mL) as fast as possible
opts.dose: 20 mL/kg (160 mL) as fast as possible

opts.r: Too little: 10 mL/kg boluses, reassessing after each.
Hypertonic 50% glucose damages infant veins: 10% glucose 2 mL/kg.

steps.label: Drug cart
steps.hint: Still shocked: more fluid, checking the liver and chest each time.

opts.t: Crystalloid second and third 10 mL/kg boluses, checking liver and chest
opts.dose: second and third 10 mL/kg boluses, checking liver and chest

steps.label: Drug cart
steps.hint: Fluid-refractory at 40 mL/kg: an inotrope, and PICU.

opts.early: Not until he has had 40 mL/kg.

opts.r: A cardiac-arrest dose into a beating heart: an infusion, 0.05–0.1 microgram/kg/min.

steps.label: Talk to his mother
steps.hint: Honest, simple, brief; she can stay.

turns.line: Is he going to die? What's happening?
turns.lz: 佢會唔會死㗎？發生咩事？

opts.t: He is very unwell with a serious blood infection. We are giving antibiotics and fluids now, and the intensive care team is coming. You can stay with him.
opts.tz: 佢而家好唔妥，血液有嚴重細菌感染。我哋而家即刻俾抗生素同埋吊鹽水，深切治療部嘅醫生都嚟緊。你可以留喺佢身邊。
opts.mark: Explains honestly and simply; lets the parent stay

opts.t: PICU and retrieval: 8 kg infant, meningococcal septic shock, 40 mL/kg, adrenaline running
opts.mark: Refers to PICU/retrieval with a clear summary

opts.t: Notify public health for contact prophylaxis

qs.q: Fluid bolus volume in paediatric septic shock (RCUK/NICE)?

qs.a: Shock and raised-ICP signs; it would delay care
wrong: He is too young for a lumbar puncture
The purpuric rash confirms meningitis, so it adds nothing
Lumbar puncture is never done in infants

badge.name: Glass Test
badge.flavor: Non-blanching and floppy: antibiotics now, 10 mL/kg and reassess.

cards.why: Reassess for response and overload after each bolus.

cards.q: Antibiotic for suspected meningococcal sepsis in a child?
cards.why: Give within an hour; don't wait for tests.

cards.q: Glucose for hypoglycaemia in a child?
APLS weight formula for under 1 year?
Sign of fluid overload during boluses?
options: Falling heart rate and warm hands
Warm peripheries and a bounding pulse

cards.q: Vasoactive drug of choice for cold septic shock in children?
cards.why: Can run peripherally/IO at low concentration until central access.
